attributes.probed_form: Loop body baseline: `c4 += 8; value = c1 + 8; value += c4; c2 += c5; c2 += 16; *(u32*)(out + i * 4) = (value << 8 | (u32)c2 << 24) | ((u32)(c0 + 16) | (u32)(c3 + 16) << 16);`.  AXIS 1, c2 group hoisted above the c1/c4 group (`c2 += c5; c2 += 16; c4 += 8; value = c1 + 8; value += c4;`) -> REGRESSED real 30 -> 46.  AXIS 2, all mutation removed (`value = (c1 + 8) + (c4 + 8);` and `(u32)(c2 + c5 + 16) << 24` inline) -> real 29 but insns fell to O46 and multiset to 1t: MWCC folds (c1+8)+(c4+8) to c1+c4+16, losing a word.  AXIS 3, THE RETAINED-THEN-REVERTED ONE, c1/c4 mutation kept and only c2's removed (`c4 += 8; value = c1 + 8; value += c4;` with `(u32)(c2 + c5 + 16) << 24` inline) -> real 30 -> 24 at T47/O47 with multiset back to IDENTICAL.  AXIS 4, symmetric mutation (`c1 += 8; c4 += 8; value = c1 + c4;`) -> REGRESSED real 29, O46, folded again.  AXIS 5, casts to block the fold (`value = (u32)(c1 + 8) + (u32)(c4 + 8);`) -> real 29, O46, byte-identical result to axis 4, which kills the fold axis by the two-identical-A/B rule.
attributes.residual: A REAL MECHANISM WAS FOUND AND IT IS WORTH CARRYING EVEN THOUGH THE CHANGE WAS REVERTED: MUTATING A LOCAL MAKES IT JUMP THE DIVISION-COMPLETION QUEUE. The six palette terms c1,c4,c2,c5,c0,c3 are independent `(u32)param_2[k] * 224 / N` chains, and the target completes them in EXACTLY the source declaration order c1,c4,c2,c5,c0,c3. Our baseline completed c2 FIRST -- c2 being the one term the source mutates (`c2 += c5; c2 += 16;`). Removing only that mutation put the completion order right and made the first sixteen instructions (0x14-0x3c) byte-identical where they had been register-mismatched, worth real 30 -> 24 at unchanged T47/O47 and multiset IDENTICAL. WHY IT WAS REVERTED ANYWAY, which is the more important half: objdiff fuzzy for the function fell 80.85107 -> 71.8936 and Game Code fuzzy 97.79 -> 97.78. Instruction-count parity was ALREADY 47/47 before the change and was still 47/47 after, so claim.law.insn-count-parity-outranks-local-opcode-fidelity's test selects FUZZY as the arbiter, and fuzzy says regression. Reading the aligned diff confirms the mechanism behind the split verdict: the change converted six opcode-only rows at the front into exact rows but opened four ours-only inserted rows in the middle, trading partial-credit rows for zero-credit ones -- `real` counts rows and improves, fuzzy weights them and worsens. NOTE FOR THE NEXT SESSION, because this is the trap: probe.py reported IMPROVED and defake_gate reported GATE OK on this change, and --update-improved banked it as the new baseline; the gate chain alone would have committed a fuzzy regression, and undoing that needed defake_gate --arbitrate plus a fresh `baseline` call. The remaining residual is the value arithmetic's PLACEMENT: target computes `addi c1+8 / addi c4+8 / add` as three adjacent instructions late (0x80-0x88); ours splits them (0x4c, 0x50, 0x88). Both fold axes are dead; the untried axis is a form that delays the value computation without changing the or-tree.
